GUANGZHOU — reported from a factory that also, apparently, walks

ROBOTS — An electric-vehicle maker's robotics arm raised more than $900 million in its first outside funding round, valuing the walking-robot business at over $6.3 billion — proving that in 2026 the fastest way to raise money is to take whatever you already make and bolt legs onto it.

"We see enormous synergy," investors said, of a company that started with cars and pivoted to humanoids, presumably because the cars kept asking for it. Analysts note the humanoid-robot gold rush has officially reached the stage where a business can be worth billions before a single one of its products has folded a single towel.
